identification.summary: ShaggyPanther is a China-linked cluster named by Kaspersky that targets government entities mainly in Taiwan and Malaysia [S3][S4]. The MISP galaxy entry states it has been active since 2008, hides encrypted payloads in registry keys, and has been seen in Indonesia and Syria [S3].
identification.firstObserved: The MISP galaxy entry says active since 2008 [S3]; this is not verified against a primary Kaspersky text. Kaspersky coverage dates from 2018 [S4].
identification.notes: Kaspersky name. No Microsoft name is mapped in this record.

attribution.confidence: Kaspersky's quarterly reporting, as relayed by secondary coverage, groups ShaggyPanther with Chinese-speaking activity [S4]. The MISP galaxy entry records country CN [S3]. No government attribution found.
attribution.basis: Kaspersky APT reporting relayed by secondary sources [S3][S4]. Underlying indicators not reviewed.

targeting.notes: Government entities are the stated focus [S3][S4].

capabilities.summary: The MISP galaxy entry states the group hides encrypted payloads in registry keys [S3]. No malware families or infrastructure were found in the sources reviewed.

campaigns.name: Kaspersky Q1 2018 APT trends mention
campaigns.summary: Coverage of Kaspersky's Q1 2018 report lists ShaggyPanther within a rise in Chinese-speaking activity, targeting government entities mainly in Taiwan and Malaysia [S4].

campaigns.name: Added to MISP galaxy
campaigns.summary: MISP galaxy added the actor with country CN, citing Kaspersky reviews from 2018-2019 [S3].

diamond.capability: Encrypted payloads hidden in registry keys [S3].
diamond.victim: Government entities in Taiwan and Malaysia; also Indonesia and Syria [S3][S4].
diamond.technology: Windows hosts, where registry-resident payloads are used [S3].
